\par\smallskip{\footnotesize\raggedright\noindent\textit{Notes.} One row per deployed atlas attribute, on the film/television side of the instrument, grouped by construct (161 attributes in all; 52 structure, 2 setting, 5 story-shape, 6 conflict, 9 character-arc, 1 narration, 31 mood, 18 genre, 37 texture). \textbf{Scale} is the native response range the instrument returns. \textbf{Valid.} is the validation of the instrument against human judgment: for the structure, setting, story-shape, conflict, narration, and texture constructs, the zero-shot Pearson correlation $r$ between the instrument's score and the human work-mean (film $r$; where a book value is shown it follows the slash and is the reader-survey $r$), estimated on the survey samples of several hundred works. The world-type and plot attributes ($^{\P}$) reproduce the base-survey values reported in the main-text validation table; the remaining structure and texture entries are the correlations of the deployed prompts, computed the same way. $^{\S}$ genre is validated as the area under the ROC curve against the human-assigned IMDb genre label rather than as a correlation, at a median AUC of 0.91 for film (and 0.93 against the reader-survey genre question for the novel). $^{\ddagger}$ each mood is validated per tone against the survey mood ratings, 28 of 31 clearing $r>0.22$ at a layer median of $r=0.41$ (0.48 on the book side); for compactness the table prints this layer median in every mood row rather than the individual per-tone value. $^{\dagger}$ the character-arc construct validates on the \emph{change} in each trait between the beginning and end of the story, at $r=0.45$--$0.54$ (9 of 9); the range printed in every arc row is this change-based validation, and the individual beginning/middle/end scores are not separately validated. \textbf{Tier} grades validation strength; tier A (strongest) and tier B clear the validation bar, while tier C attributes fall below it and are disclosed but read with caution. The fifteen structural attributes marked $^{\P}$ additionally clear the bar in both film and the reader survey and carry the cross-medium geometry; additional non-structural attributes also validate in both media (the two settings, the Cinderella, Rags to Riches, and Riches to Rags story shapes, and the conflict types), but the cross-medium comparisons rest on the fifteen structural attributes, elicited on scales identical across the two media. Across the nine constructs 150 of the 161 scored attributes validate.\par}}
